newsitem.title: CHINA: Germany's Herzog expects frank talks with China.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Herzog expects frank talks with China.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog arrived in Beijing on Monday for a week-long state visit, during which he is expected to raise China's human rights record.
"I will have very frank talks," Herzog told reporters during a sunny but windblown visit to the Great Wall in rural Beijing after his arrival.

Herzog has said he plans to raise the sensitive subject of Beijing's human rights record as well as economic, cultural and scientific issues during talks with Chinese counterpart Jiang Zemin, Premier Li Peng and other senior leaders.
Herzog, who has been under pressure in Germany to stress human rights after a recent crackdown on dissent by Beijing authorities, declined to give any details of the expected content of his talks.
He has said he will not keep silent on "critical issues" during meetings with Chinese leaders, but also that the conversations will not be made public.
Last week, a Chinese court rejected the appeal of dissident and former student leader Wang Dan and upheld an 11-year jail term for plotting to subvert the government.
The sentence was the latest in a series of blows to China's struggling democracy movement.

During a visit to China last month that had been long delayed by a dispute over Tibet, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said Beijing and Bonn had put their differences behind them and had set a course for expanded economic ties.
